messages:
Maya R.: FYI I opened a tiny docs PR to add an alternate egress pattern for Private installs that must DNAT through a customer NAT gateway and preserve SNI. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/2001 :link:  

Anil K.: Nice — can we show both nftables and iptables examples? Some customers still ask for iptables snippets. Also include a short explanation for why preserving SNI matters when KMS does TLS hostname validation.

Maya R.: Added both. Key points I added:
- Envoy setting to preserve SNI: `use_remote_address` not enough; set `sni` in the upstream cluster tls context.
- nftables DNAT example for gateway-forwarding + conntrack helper notes.
- iptables translation for legacy installs.

Snippet I dropped in the PR for Envoy upstream cluster TLS SNI:

```yaml
clusters:
  - name: kms-cluster
    connect_timeout: 5s
    tls_context:
      common_tls_context:
        tls_certificates:
          - certificate_chain: { filename: "/etc/redwood/certs/client.crt" }
            private_key: { filename: "/etc/redwood/certs/client.key" }
    sni: "kms.internal.example.com"
```

Priya (docs): Can you add a one-line rationale: "Set `sni` to the DNS name the KMS expects so upstream certs validate the hostname." That'll help less-experienced readers. Also, please add a KB snippet for Support showing how to verify SNI with `openssl s_client -servername`.

Jorge: Pasted the nftables DNAT example I tested with our sealed-site lab:

```bash
# forward 443 to NAT gateway at 10.0.0.1
nft add table ip redwood_nat
nft add chain ip redwood_nat prerouting { type nat hook prerouting priority 0 ; }
nft add rule ip redwood_nat prerouting tcp dport 443 dnat to 10.0.0.1:443
```

And the iptables equivalent:

```bash
iptables -t nat -A PREROUTING -p tcp --dport 443 -j DNAT --to-destination 10.0.0.1:443
```

Maya R.: I also included a short note about conntrack: for long-lived connections (kms gRPC streams) bump `nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established` on gateways to avoid mid-stream drops. Added file-perms/ownership for bundled certs in air-gapped tarball (`chown root:root && chmod 600 client.key`).

Anil K.: Tiny nit: call out the order of CA + intermediates in the bundled `ca_bundle.pem` and recommend path `/etc/redwood/certs/ca_bundle.pem`. Otherwise Support tickets show `certificate signed by unknown authority`.

Priya (docs): I'll clean wording and add a "Troubleshooting quick checks" box: SNI, CA bundle order, file permissions, conntrack timeouts, and dns resolution on the NAT gateway. Also create a short KB for Support with the `openssl` and `curl --resolve` examples.

Ops Bot: preflight-run started: docs-pr-2001 - egress-sni-dnat 4BB status: queued

Jorge: One more test I ran for air-gapped customers: include the CA bundle inside the installer and set env var `REDWOOD_KMS_CA=/etc/redwood/certs/ca_bundle.pem` in the packaged systemd unit. Example systemd snippet I pushed:

```ini
[Service]
Environment=REDWOOD_KMS_CA=/etc/redwood/certs/ca_bundle.pem
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/redwood-agent --config /etc/redwood/config.yaml
Restart=on-failure
```

Maya R.: Great. I added a short paragraph about validating SNI post-install with this command:

```
openssl s_client -connect kms.internal.example.com:443 -servername kms.internal.example.com -showcerts -CAfile /etc/redwood/certs/ca_bundle.pem
```

Priya (docs): Ops Bot says preflight passed, leaving one stylistic nit about using consistent `kms.internal.example.com` vs `kms.example.local`. I'll standardize names and merge after that.
